messages.content: Bind the generative model to the inference serving contract. Identify the model identifier 'synthetic-review-summarizer-v1' and the serving endpoint 'https://inference.example.com/v1/chat/completions'. Record the effective model name and endpoint.

I'll bind the generative model to its inference serving contract by recording the model identifier and endpoint, with some light validation of the contract fields.

```python
import pandas as pd
from urllib.parse import urlparse

# --- Declared serving contract inputs ---
model_identifier = "synthetic-review-summarizer-v1"
serving_endpoint = "https://inference.example.com/v1/chat/completions"

# --- Validate / normalize the endpoint ---
parsed = urlparse(serving_endpoint)
endpoint_valid = all([parsed.scheme == "https", bool(parsed.netloc), parsed.path.endswith("/v1/chat/completions")])

# --- Bind model -> serving contract ---
binding = {
    "effective_model_name": model_identifier,
    "endpoint": serving_endpoint,
    "endpoint_host": parsed.netloc,
    "endpoint_path": parsed.path,
    "transport": parsed.scheme,
    "api_style": "openai-compatible chat completions",
    "endpoint_valid": endpoint_valid,
    "contract_status": "bound" if endpoint_valid else "invalid_endpoint",
}

contract_df = pd.DataFrame([binding]).set_index("effective_model_name")
print(contract_df.T)
```
